documents.title: Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.
documents.abstract: Ischemic stroke and ischemic acute kidney injury are both clinical challenges. Danhong injection (DHI) has been reported to exert protective effects against cerebral and renal ischemic injury. However, the shared therapeutic targets and mechanisms underlying its effects in these two organs remain unclear. Using network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro experiments, this study investigated shared targets and pathways associated with cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and evaluated whether DHI exerted a shared ferroptosis-related endot

documents.title: Efficient flavonoids from Helichrysum bracteatum and their multi-target antioxidant mechanisms.
documents.abstract: Helichrysum bracteatum is a promising source of natural antioxidants for food preservation. However, unclear mechanisms and inefficient extraction limit the application of its flavonoids in functional foods. Here, we report a response surface methodology (RSM)-optimized hydroethanolic reflux extraction yielding a maximum flavonoid extraction yield of 16.0% under optimized conditions (27: 1 mL/g, 68% ethanol, 1.6 h). The major flavonoids identified were quercetin (29.44%), kaempferol (8.03%), and rutin (3.44%), and the extract exhibited strong radical-scavenging activity. Network analysis ident

documents.title: Membrane lipid-driven gating of TREK-1 channels: Revisiting anesthetic mechanisms beyond protein targets.
documents.abstract: The mechanistic basis of general anesthesia has long been debated between protein-centric and lipid-centric frameworks, and the TWIK-related potassium channel 1 (TREK-1), a member of the two-pore domain K+ (K2P) superfamily, sits at the intersection of the two as a physiologically relevant target of both volatile and intravenous anesthetics. Although the direct interaction of anesthetics with TREK-1 protein has been studied extensively, how membrane lipid composition and lipid-driven conformational dynamics modulate channel gating remains insufficiently explored. documents.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.
documents.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure-activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. documents.title: Mechanisms of Hofmeister ion effects on protein properties and their applications in food protein processing: A review.
documents.abstract: The Hofmeister series is a fundamental paradigm for ion-specific regulation of protein properties, with anions playing a dominant role. However, its molecular mechanism remains long-debated, and a systematic synthesis linking basic theory to food protein processing practices is still lacking. This review dissects the action mechanisms of Hofmeister anions from water structure regulation and ion-protein interactions, and summarizes their applications in protein extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization and structural modification. documents.title: Structure-based binding pocket conservation analysis identifies 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase candidates across phylogenetically diverse bacteria.
documents.abstract: Urolithins are polyphenolic compounds produced by gut microbiota from dietary ellagitannins and ellagic acid, with urolithin A being the most bioactive and associated with a range of pharmaceutical activities like anti-aging and anti-inflammatory effects. Despite these benefits, the number of known urolithin A-producing bacteria and their corresponding enzymes is very limited. documents.title: AlphaFold models of host-pathogen interactions elucidate the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry.
documents.abstract: Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall

documents.title: Large-scale analysis of AlphaFold structures reveals organism-specific physicochemical signatures.
documents.abstract: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures. Our analysis revealed systematic variation between proteins from different organisms to such an extent that major features of the tree of life could be recovered from these data. Surprisingly, this relationship persisted even when we restricted our analysis to euk

documents.title: Effect of amino acid substitutions on the structure and dynamics of human PRPP synthetase PRPS1.
documents.abstract: Phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP), is required for the synthesis of nucleotides and mutations in human PRPP synthetase (hPRPS1) are linked to Arts syndrome and X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 5. Here, we investigated mutations linked to these neurological diseases using molecular dynamics simulations. We highlight small but measurable correlations between structural change and kinetic properties as demonstrated by mutant A190V, which exhibits reduced feedback inhibition by ADP and GDP, consistent with superactivity of PRPS1. Changes in RMSD and Rg indicate increased flexibility of mutant Q1

documents.title: Network pharmacology and molecular dynamics uncover RMJ's targets and mechanisms for treating atherosclerosis.
documents.abstract: Atherosclerosis involves complex pathogenesis including inflammation, lipid disorders, and abnormal autophagy, yet current treatments are limited by adverse reactions and drug resistance, highlighting the need for novel strategies.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Natural Product Pharmacology: From Molecular Discovery to Precision Therapeutics.
documents.abstract: The use of natural products as a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules for drug development has been well established; however, their multicomponent and multitarget nature, uncertain target causality, variable in vivo exposure, and heterogeneous responses to therapy make them challenging to characterize pharmacologically and translate into clinical practice. Systems pharmacology, together with artificial intelligence (AI), provides new approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, integration of multidimensional data, and development of precision therapeutics. documents.title: GNG2-MRAS interaction regulates SHOC2-dependent RAF activation and MAPK signaling.
documents.abstract: Dysregulation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway is a hallmark of many human cancers and RASopathies. The SHOC2-MRAS-PP1Cα (SMP) holophosphatase complex is a crucial regulatory node of this pathway. It activates the MAPK pathway by dephosphorylating the inhibitory phosphoserine on RAF kinases and thereby relieving RAF autoinhibition. Although GNG2, the γ-subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, has recently emerged as a negative modulator of MAPK signaling, its molecular mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. documents.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Natural Products: Potential Effects on Mitochondrial Energy Metabolism in Heart Failure.
documents.abstract: Heart failure (HF), the end-stage of cardiovascular disease (CVD), affects over 64 million people globally. There is an alarming trend of earlier onset, which poses a substantial healthcare burden. Although guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) has significantly improved clinical outcomes, residual morbidity and mortality remain considerable, highlighting the need for additional therapeutic strategies. Mitochondrial energy metabolism (MEM) plays an important role in HF pathophysiology and represents a potential therapeutic target. Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived natural products (TCM-

documents.title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.
documents.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein-ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. documents.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

documents.title: Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.
documents.abstract: Enzymes are indispensable biocatalysts in industrial processes, but their application is often restricted by narrow pH optima. Exposure to acidic or alkaline conditions alters the protonation states of ionizable residues, disrupts catalytic microenvironments and stabilizing interactions, and ultimately reduces activity, catalytic efficiency, or structural integrity. This limitation is particularly important in industrial sectors such as detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations, where operation under non-native pH conditions is frequently required. documents.title: CovPDB 2.0: an expanded covalent protein-ligand interactome.
documents.abstract: The rational design of covalently binding inhibitors to specifically block selected target proteins has become a common strategy in drug discovery. Such design is based on structural insights into how electrophilic ligands bind to nucleophilic residues. CovPDB v1.0 provided high-resolution cocrystal structures of biologically relevant covalent protein-ligand complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank. documents.title: GO- and calcium silicate NP-modified diamides for enhanced antimicrobial activity: structural, morphological, and in silico investigations.
documents.abstract: We herein report the preparation and investigation of antimicrobial nanohybrid systems based on antimicrobial diamides and GO, as well as CaSiO3 NPs. Diamides were synthesized by condensation of 4-nitrobenzoyl chloride with aromatic diamines under catalyst-free conditions, followed by non-covalent conjugation of the obtained compounds with GO and CaSiO3. Synthesized diamides, NPs, and nanoensembles were investigated by spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction techniques. The obtained two-component nanohybrid systems were examined against bacterial and yeast strains, which demonstrated their

documents.title: Pyrazolyl-triazolyl chalcones as promising antimycobacterial candidates: integrating experimental and computational insights.
documents.abstract: In pursuit of developing novel antitubercular scaffolds, a series of pyrazolyl-triazolyl-functionalized chalcones (6a-o) were synthesized and evaluated for their antimycobacterial activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv using the MABA assay. The synthesized compounds exhibited promising inhibitory potential, with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values ranging from 1.6 to 12.5 µg mL-1. Among them, compounds 6b and 6k emerged as the most potent analogues (MIC = 1.6 µg mL-1), followed by compounds 6c, 6d, 6g, 6h, 6j, and 6l displaying strong activity (MIC = 3.12 µg mL-1). Molecul

documents.title: Water-network reorganization upon ligand binding in BRD4 bromodomains: An integrated hydration-site analysis.
documents.abstract: Water molecules play critical roles in ligand binding to BRD4 bromodomains (BD1 and BD2). Although crystallographic studies have provided extensive structural information on these water molecules, how water-mediated interactions reorganize under different ligand-binding conditions remains poorly understood. Here, we performed an integrated characterization of hydration sites based on crystal structures and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate water-mediated interactions and network reorganizations associated with ligand binding. documents.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
documents.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. documents.title: Conformational Plasticity of Orthosteric Pocket Enables the Discovery of a Novel PAD4-Selective Inhibitor.
documents.abstract: Peptidyl-arginine deiminase (PAD) family enzymes are pivotal enzymes that catalyze the citrullination of arginine in substrate proteins. Elevated levels of citrullinated proteins are tightly linked to the incidence of rheumatoid arthritis, neurodegenerative diseases, and cancers, thus highlighting PAD enzymes as important therapeutic targets. Although several PAD isozyme-selective and non-selective small molecule inhibitors have been reported over the last decade, it remains important to identify distinct ligands that may offer differentiated therapeutic potential or selectivity. documents.title: Nanomaterial-based glucose sensors: detection platforms and highlight applications.
documents.abstract: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved into a severe global public health crisis. Precise, rapid, and stable glucose monitoring is therefore indispensable for the early diagnosis, clinical intervention, and long-term management of diabetes. Conventional enzyme-dependent glucose sensors suffer from inherent limitations, including high manufacturing costs, inferior environmental stability, short serv

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing.
documents.abstract: Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. documents.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
documents.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. documents.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21-CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach.
documents.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite's secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21-CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host-parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate bin

documents.title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF6 Alternative Insulating Gas.
documents.abstract: HFO-1336mzz-(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz-(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. Acute inhal

documents.title: Investigating Ferritin Permeability to Metal-Based Drugs through Molecular Dynamics.
documents.abstract: In this study, we implemented a workflow based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess whether gold-(I)-containing complexes can traverse the C3 channels of human H ferritin and which energetic barriers were at play in the process. By using two example complexes for which an extensive experimental characterization was already available, we observed that classical MD correctly indicated which one could spontaneously pass through the channel. documents.title: Solving the Computational Peptide Design Puzzle: Challenges and Opportunities.
documents.abstract: Peptides are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutics, antimicrobial agents, and supramolecular biomaterials due to the remarkable versatility encoded in their amino acid sequences. However, the rational design of peptides remains challenging because sequence-structure-function relationships are not yet fully understood. Experimental exploration of peptide chemical space is inherently limited by the vast number of possible sequences and the complexity of resolving peptide behavior at molecular resolution. documents.title: Structural Characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ Reveals Membrane-Dependent Stabilization of Its Conserved Electron-Transfer Cofactor Network.
documents.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence in granulomas depends on lipid catabolism through the β-oxidation-coupled respiratory pathway, which requires the essential membrane-associated protein IspQ, encoded by Rv0338c. Although IspQ is a genetically and chemically validated drug target, its structural organization and membrane-dependent function remain unknown. documents.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes.
documents.abstract: Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. documents.title: Prospects of time-resolved vibrational electron energy loss spectroscopy: A FTE-TACAW method.
documents.abstract: Seeing that ultrafast (picosecond timescale) vibrational electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) should soon be experimentally realizable, we present an in silico approach capable of providing insight from the computational physics perspective. We present a framework that combines frozen trajectory excitation (FTE) with time auto-correlation of auxiliary wavefunctions (TACAW) to study the time-dependent spectral response of non-equilibrium lattice dynamics in a way comparable directly to experiment-(scanning) transmission electron microscope EELS, (S)TEM-EELS. documents.title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2‑Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method.
documents.abstract: Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. documents.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
documents.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. documents.title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.
documents.abstract: Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment-protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic-vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. documents.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters

documents.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
documents.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. documents.title: Structure-based discovery of new GPR119 ligands from on-demand tera-scale chemical space.
documents.abstract: The orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR119 is involved in glucose homeostasis and is considered a promising target for the treatment of diabetes and other metabolic diseases. The recently solved structures of GPR119 in complex with potential endogenous lipid agonists, including oleoylethanolamide (OEA), provide a solid platform for 3D pharmacology analysis and structure-based ligand discovery. Here, we employed the V-SYNTHES2 approach to screen ∼3 trillion on-demand compounds from Enamine xREAL chemical space to identify several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. documents.title: Structure-Based Discovery of GTP-Enhanced Rab10 Modulators and Their Effects on Alzheimer's Disease-Relevant Cellular Phenotypes.
documents.abstract: Rab10-mediated membrane trafficking has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but pharmacological tools for investigating its function remain limited. Here, we screened more than 80 million compounds using structure-based virtual screening and prioritized five candidate Rab10 modulators ( R1-R5 ). These compounds exhibited favorable docking scores, stable modeled protein-ligand complexes in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and predicted acceptable ADME/toxicity profiles. documents.title: Large-Scale Prospective Virtual Screening Using a Co-Folding-Rescoring Workflow for NPM1-TYK2 Inhibitor Discovery.
documents.abstract: Conventional large-scale structure-based virtual screening typically relies on fixed-receptor docking, in which ligand poses are sampled against a predefined receptor conformation. Protein-ligand co-folding models can instead generate candidate complex conformations by jointly modeling ligand placement and local receptor-ligand structural adaptation. documents.title: Pharmacological Mechanisms of Action and Therapeutic Basis of Qihuang Jianpi Zishen Granules in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Study Integrating Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Experimental Validation.
documents.abstract: This study aimed to clarify the material basis and mechanism by which Qihuang Jianpi Zishen granules (QHJPZSG) treat systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). UPLC-Q-TOF-MSE was used to characterize the chemical constituents of QHJPZSG and its serum-absorbed components in rats. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were applied to screen key active compounds, potential targets, and signaling pathways, followed by in vivo validation using MRL/lpr mice and in vitro verification with primary B cells. documents.title: Diversity at the Acinetobacter baumannii K locus: towards a comprehensive database for in silico prediction of capsular polysaccharide types.
documents.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is one of the most critical bacterial pathogens requiring novel approaches for infection control and treatment to curb the spread of highly resistant isolates. Epidemiological surveillance and the design and application of many non-antibiotic interventions require rapid and accurate prediction of diverse capsular polysaccharide (CPS) types from whole-genome sequence data. documents.title: Structural Determinants of Biologic Recognition Across GPCR Classes.
documents.abstract: The rapid increase in experimentally resolved G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-biologic complexes has substantially improved our understanding of the molecular basis of receptor recognition and modulation. However, despite the growing number of available structures, a comparative framework integrating the major GPCR classes is still lacking. In this review, we analysed experimentally resolved GPCR-biologic complexes across receptor Classes A, B, C, and F to identify the structural principles governing biologic recognition. documents.title: An OGE-HPLC-ABTS-Q-TOF MS Screening of Antioxidant Components in Gushuning Tablet (GSN) With Computational Prediction of Related Biological Targets.
documents.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a severe skeletal disorder that poses a major threat to public health, and oxidative stress may be one of its core pathological mechanisms. The Traditional Chinese Medicine compound preparation Gushuning Tablet (GSN) has been reported to show potential clinical benefits in OP, potentially related to the modulation of OP-associated oxidative stress. However, its antioxidant active material basis and mechanism of action remain unclear. documents.title: Inhibition of quorum sensing and biofilm in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by erythrinin B: Bioinformatic evidence for the LasR binding.
documents.abstract: Quorum sensing (QS)-regulated virulence factors and biofilm formation are major contributors to antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This highlights the urgent need for novel anti-virulence strategies that can disrupt these pathways and reduce such infections. The objective of this study was to evaluate the inhibitory potential of erythrinin B against QS-regulated virulence factors and biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa PAO1. documents.title: Identification of novel compounds from Olea Europaea targeting hDus2 as potential anticancer agents: a molecular docking and molecular dynamics study.
documents.abstract: Leukemia, a type of blood cancer, ranks among the top causes of cancer-related fatalities. Human tRNA-dihydrouridine synthase 2 (hDus2) catalyzes the conversion of uridine to dihydrouridine in the tRNA and is overexpressed in cancer cells, facilitating the translational process required for cancer cell growth. Inhibition of hDus2 reduces cancer cell growth and viability while increasing apoptosis sensitivity under stress, making it an excellent cancer target. documents.title: SLC38A2-Driven Glutamine Metabolic Reprogramming Promotes Hypoxic Survival in Glioblastoma.
documents.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is highly refractory to standard therapies, including anti-angiogenic agents such as bevacizumab. While bevacizumab prunes tumor vasculature, it exacerbates intratumoral hypoxia, which drives a metabolically resilient phenotype that limits survival benefits. This study aimed to identify the metabolic dependencies underlying GBM adaptation to hypoxia and to evaluate whether targeting these dependencies could enhance the antitumor efficacy of bevacizumab. documents.title: Advances in injectable liposome-microspheres platforms for osteoarthritis therapy: from sustained delivery to multifunctional disease modification.
documents.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, whole-joint disorder marked by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, and capsular fibrosis, affecting over 500 million individuals worldwide. Current pharmacotherapies are mainly palliative, with no approved disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs). Intra-articular (IA) injection provides direct joint access but is hampered by rapid drug clearance and short residence times. documents.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
documents.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. documents.title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies.
documents.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. However, the concurrent challenges of implant-associated bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration remain formidable obstacles in clinical practice.
